items.stem: What does LoRA change during fine-tuning?

options.text: It trains small low-rank adapter matrices while the base weights stay frozen
options.rationale: Correct: LoRA learns low-rank updates and leaves the base weights unchanged.

options.text: It retrains every weight in the base model
options.rationale: That is full fine-tuning; LoRA freezes the base.
LoRA adds adapters to layers, not vocabulary entries.

options.text: It increases the model's context window
options.rationale: Context length is unrelated to LoRA adapters.

items.stem: Which TWO are advantages of parameter-efficient fine-tuning over full fine-tuning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Much lower GPU memory and storage requirements
options.rationale: Correct: only small adapters are trained and stored.

options.text: Easy swapping of task-specific adapters on one base model
options.rationale: Correct: adapters can be attached or detached per task.

options.text: It removes the need for any training data
It always reaches higher accuracy than full fine-tuning
options.rationale: Full fine-tuning can match or exceed PEFT; PEFT trades a little quality for efficiency.

items.explanation: Correct: only small adapters are trained and stored.

items.stem: After fine-tuning, the model follows the new style but now fails tasks it used to handle. What is this called?

options.rationale: Correct: the model has lost prior general ability while adapting to new data.
That arises from low-precision numerics, not fine-tuning drift.
That is a vocabulary issue, not loss of general ability.
Leakage inflates evaluation scores; it is not loss of prior ability.
